title: An Indian Family’s Dal Makhani Finds a Home on the French Riviera
excerpt: The family-run Mantraah in Nice’s Old Town serves dal makhani, tandoori naan and paneer to rave reviews — including repeat dinners three nights running.
body:
• An Indian family has opened Mantraah, an Indian restaurant in the Old Town of Nice on the French Riviera, at 2 Place de la Halle aux Herbes near the Nice Cathedral.
  • A viral Instagram video — “POV: your family opened an Indian restaurant on the French Riviera” — shows diners enjoying dal makhani, tandoori naan, paneer, biryani and tandoori dishes, with children helping serve “with utmost affection.”
  • Customers have left glowing reviews, from repeat dinners three nights running to praise for the lassi and nimbu paani.
  • Mantraah is open daily from 11:45 AM to 11 PM at moderate prices, pitching “authentic Indian cuisine with a refined, modern touch — in the heart of Nice.”

The French Riviera is famous for ratatouille and salade niçoise. Now, in the Old Town of Nice, a family-run Indian restaurant is serving up dal makhani and tandoori naan to crowds of locals and tourists — and the internet has noticed.

Mantraah, at 2 Place de la Halle aux Herbes near the Nice Cathedral, is the project of an Indian family who decided to bring their home cuisine to the Côte d’Azur. The restaurant shared an Instagram video with the text overlay “POV: your family opened an Indian restaurant on the French Riviera,” and the clips — diners digging into naan, cream-topped curries, paneer preparations, rice, tandoori dishes, chicken, biryani, papads, chutneys and fresh coriander — struck a chord. In the video, children who appear to be part of the family are seen serving food “with utmost affection,” according to NDTV Food.

“The food was truly so so good! I wish I’d gotten the lassi recipe!”

— A customer review quoted by NDTV Food

Repeat customers, rave reviews

The reviews read like a love letter. One diner wrote that they “went there three days straight for dinner,” praising “most welcoming staff, warm hospitality and food, omg the flavours and the quality.” Another said simply: “Food was so good that we are here twice on our trip!” Several called out the beverages — especially the lassi and nimbu paani — and one declared the children the “cutest serving staff.”

Mantraah positions itself as “authentic Indian cuisine with a refined, modern touch — in the heart of Nice,” and is open daily from 11:45 AM to 11 PM. The restaurant is described as newly opened, with a review volume consistent with a 2026 debut.

A diaspora comfort-food story

For Indians abroad, missing home food is a near-universal experience — and Indian families keep answering it by opening restaurants in unexpected corners of the world. Mantraah fits the pattern: a family bet that French Riviera tourists, raised on Provençal cuisine, will embrace dal makhani.

The early signs suggest the bet is working. In a city better known for seafood bouillabaisse than butter chicken, an Indian family’s tandoori is drawing customers back for second and third dinners. For the diaspora audience scrolling from afar, it is the kind of feel-good story that makes a continent feel closer to home.
